draft.title: Newton's second law
card: The net force is the total of all forces on an object, found by adding forces along a line and taking their directions into account. Newton's second law says net force = mass × acceleration, or F = ma.
Force is in newtons (N), mass in kilograms (kg) and acceleration in metres per second squared (m/s²). One newton gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².
The acceleration points in the same direction as the net force. For the same net force, a larger mass gives a smaller acceleration.
If the net force is zero, the acceleration is zero. If several forces act, first add them along the line, taking their directions into account, then use F = ma on the net force.
draft.remember: Acceleration depends on the net force and the mass, not on any single force.

a.q: A trolley has a mass of 3 kg. A net force of 12 N pushes it to the right. What is its acceleration?
opts: 4 m/s² in the direction of the net force
4 m/s² opposite to the net force
36 m/s² in the direction of the net force
0.25 m/s² in the direction of the net force
a.why: a = F ÷ m = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 m/s², and it points in the direction of the net force. Multiplying 12 by 3 to get 36 is the tempting mistake, because it ignores that acceleration is force divided by mass.
a.clue: Divide the net force by the mass.

b.q: Priya pushes a 20 kg box east with a force of 50 N. Friction of 30 N acts west on the box. What is the acceleration of the box?
b.why: The net force is 50 N east minus 30 N west, which is 20 N east. Then a = 20 ÷ 20 = 1 m/s² east. Using the 50 N push alone gives 2.5 m/s², which ignores friction.
b.clue: Find the net force before you use F = ma.

a.best: 4 m/s² in the direction of the net force
